note: points: the tick marks, each set on its axis line as fitted through the ink. The y axis leans 0.37 deg to the left and the x axis rises 0.20 deg to the right, a skew of 0.17 deg; the x ticks close up to the right (96.5, 95.0, 92.7, 91.8, 88.0 px per 400 m; the affine fit leaves 4.0 px); curve (a) runs past the 2000 tick (impact 2058 m). The frame convention of Figs 10, 12, 13 and 14 (fig10.py): x is read between the x ticks (xgrid: the tick columns on the x axis line, piecewise linear, extended by one tick step at both ends, the end interval repeated, as a safeguard for a point past the last tick) along lines parallel to the drawn y axis (lean: the fitted axis lines, x axis row = xaxis[0] col + xaxis[1], y axis col = yaxis[0] row + yaxis[1]); y is the affine fit of the points. digitize.py reads xgrid by column alone (it ignores lean), so its overlay of these curves is off by the lean; fig10.py prints the overlay with this mapping.
